title: Automatic renal elastography quantification associates with kidney impairment
summary: nnU-Net segmentation enabled automated renal shear-wave measurements in a 179-participant MRI study. In the 106-person test set, including 59 people with chronic kidney disease, cortical stiffness was lower even with mild impairment and renal measurements correlated with eGFR. This observational imaging association does not establish causality or screening benefit; independent clinical validation remains needed.
organization: Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine; Guangzhou Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary full paper relevant model Methods, study Results and limitations; exact primary front-matter identity and Europe PMC metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Held-out segmentation and renal-stiffness/eGFR association; test set 47 controls and 59 CKD participants.
evidence.unknown: Independent diagnosis/prognosis, causal interpretation and clinical benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: nnU-Net delineates renal cortex, medulla and parenchyma; learned contours support automated elastographic measurements linked to renal-function groups.
